detailed_description: XML Validator checks whether pasted XML is well-formed by using the browser's XML parser. Paste XML into the text area, validate it, and the page reports whether parsing succeeded or shows the parser error text, with line and column details when the browser includes them. The Format action serializes valid XML and inserts line breaks and indentation for a more readable view, while Load Example fills the editor with sample catalog XML. This is a quick browser-side checker for malformed tags, nesting mistakes, and basic parsing errors; it does not check external schemas or contact a backend service.
usage_steps: Paste XML into the XML input text area.
Click Validate to run the browser parser.
Review the valid or invalid result message and any parser error text.
Use Format when the XML parses successfully and you want a more readable layout.
Use Load Example to insert sample XML for a quick smoke test.
Edit the XML and validate again until the parser accepts it.
usage_examples: Check whether a copied XML snippet has mismatched opening and closing tags.
Format a small XML configuration file before pasting it into documentation.
Debug a broken RSS or sitemap fragment by reading the browser parser error.
Load the example XML to confirm the validator is working before testing your own input.

faqs.question: Does XML Validator check XSD or DTD schemas?
faqs.answer: No. The current page checks browser XML well-formedness only.

faqs.question: Can I upload an XML file?
faqs.answer: No. Paste XML text into the editor.

faqs.question: Does Format fix invalid XML?
faqs.answer: No. Format works after the XML parses successfully; invalid XML still needs manual correction.

faqs.question: Where does validation happen?
faqs.answer: Validation happens in the browser with DOMParser, without sending the XML to a backend.
